proposed_comments.title: Centralize the binary materialization contract
proposed_comments.body:
### Centralize the binary materialization contract

**Severity:** `medium`

The binary branch currently embeds the `SoftwareBitmap` check directly in `TryCreateIconSourceSynchronously`, while the loader and tests need the same rule to decide whether asynchronous transfer is required. Please expose one shared predicate for the binary-plus-bitmap case and use it from both the synchronous conversion path and its callers so a future change cannot make those decisions disagree. Add focused coverage for the empty, URI, SVG, glyph, empty-binary, and bitmap-backed binary cases.

confidence.rationale: The fork-only change extracts the exact predicate from the current RIGHT-side binary branch and the matching tests exercise each prepared-icon kind.

proposed_comments.title: Exercise every synchronous icon-source materialization branch
proposed_comments.body:
### Exercise every synchronous icon-source materialization branch

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Tests/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.UnitTests/IconPathConverterTests.cs` — `IconSourceMaterializationContractSeparatesSynchronousKindsFromBinaryTransfer`; `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Helpers/Icons/IconPathConverter.cs` — `TryCreateIconSourceSynchronously` and the binary transfer path.

**Problem:** The current tests classify empty, bitmap URI, SVG URI, and glyph inputs only through `RequiresAsynchronousMaterialization`. They do not invoke the synchronous materialization API for those kinds, so an incorrect source type or a broken synchronous branch could still pass.

**Why it matters:** The PR changes the boundary between synchronous UI-thread construction and asynchronous bitmap transfer. Each supported synchronous kind needs a regression assertion so a later refactor cannot silently route it through the wrong path.

**Suggested change:**
1. Create one prepared icon for each empty, bitmap URI, SVG URI, and glyph input.
2. Call `TryCreateIconSourceSynchronously` for each input and assert success plus the expected `IconSource` subtype.
3. Keep separate empty-binary and bitmap-backed binary cases, asserting the bitmap ownership transfer and cleanup contract.

**Illustrative test shape:**
```csharp
Assert.IsTrue(IconPathConverter.TryCreateIconSourceSynchronously(glyph, out var source));
Assert.IsInstanceOfType<FontIconSource>(source);
```

**Verification:** Run `Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.UnitTests` in x64 Debug and confirm all materialization-contract cases pass with no leaked `SoftwareBitmap` ownership.

proposed_comments.title: Keep diagnostics assertions isolated per cache partition
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep diagnostics assertions isolated per cache partition

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Tests/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.UnitTests/IconLoadDiagnosticsTests.cs` — the cache-report test covering glyph and other partitions.

**Problem:** Once glyph and other caches are reported independently, assertions against the whole report can accidentally match values from the wrong partition and leave the new partition contract under-tested.

**Why it matters:** Diagnostics are used to compare cache behavior by source class. A report can look correct while glyph and other counters are swapped, merged, or attributed to the wrong section.

**Suggested change:**
1. Record at least one lookup, entry addition, and removal for the `Other` partition.
2. Split the report into glyph and other sections using their stable headings.
3. Assert lookup, hit/miss, maximum-entry, and removal-reason values within the matching partition section rather than across the entire report.

**Illustrative assertion shape:**
```csharp
var otherSection = GetTextBetween(report.Text, "  20x20 Other cache, capacity 16", "Request origins");
StringAssert.Contains(otherSection, "    Misses: 1");
```

**Verification:** Run the CmdPal UI unit-test project and verify that changing either partition's counters causes the corresponding section assertion to fail.
